quick.summary: Why filtering a massive table by date is still sometimes incredibly slow.
quick.takeaway: Group data into folders in advance so the database skips the wrong ones.

beats.line: I filtered my query by date, but it took twenty minutes. Why?
Because it looked at every single row anyway. Like reading every library shelf.
But I told it exactly which day I wanted.
The database did not know how the data was organized.
We have to arrange the tables by date in advance.
This is known as partition pruning.
Can I just say skipping the wrong folders?
That is perfect. The database sees the folder label and skips it.
So I arrange the data into daily folders to make searches fast.
Now you are flying straight to the right section.

quiz.question: If your query is already filtering by date, why arrange the table by date too?
options: It allows the database to completely ignore unrelated daily folders.
It turns the query into a common table expression.
It deletes old records automatically to save space.
It changes the dates into plain text formats.
quiz.explanation: Arranging it in advance means the database can skip massive amounts of data without reading it.

quiz.question: Skipping the wrong folders means you do not have to filter your query anymore.
quiz.explanation: You still must filter your query. That filter is what tells the database which folders to read and which to skip.
